title: Introduce language-aware lint profiles and presubmit throttler to reduce noisy failures
author: Samir Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit lanes have become noisy and slow for multi-language changes. Teams touching small TypeScript or Python clients were getting full-lane lint runs and long presubmit runtime even when the change only affected docs or a single language. This PR introduces language-aware lint profiles (typed configs per language and directory heuristics) plus a lightweight presubmit throttler that limits concurrent heavy-lint executions for large monorepo merges. Goals: reduce noisy failures, shorten feedback for small edits, and keep full-lint coverage for large cross-language changes.

What this changes (high level): 
- New lint profiles: .github/lint-profiles/typescript.yaml, python.yaml, go.yaml, docs.yaml. Each profile narrows enabled linters and rules tuned for the language (e.g., skip TS type-check on minor docs-only changes).
- Changed presubmit router (.github/presubmit-router.yaml): maps changed file globs to lint profiles and test subsets.
- Presubmit throttler service (internal small Go binary under tools/presubmit-throttler): in-repo controller that enforces per-branch concurrency caps and priority hints so we avoid overload spikes on CI runners.
- CI job updates: workflow presubmit.yml now selects the lint profile and conditionally runs the heavy lang-specific job. Added fast-path checks for docs-only, infra-only, or README changes.
- Backfill: helper script scripts/preview-lint-profile.sh to simulate profile selection locally.

Testing and verification: 
- Local unit tests for router logic and throttler behavior included under tools/presubmit-throttler/test/*.
- Staging CI run (workflow: presubmit-staging) exercised path matching across 40+ sample PR diffs. One flaky unit in the throttler tests was observed and rerun; CI passed on the second run.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge behind feature flag and enable for a small set of projects (redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-docs). 
2) Monitor presubmit latency and failure rate dashboards (Console -> CI -> Presubmit-latency). 
3) Gradually expand to all repos using a rollout tag in presubmit-router.yaml. 

Operational notes and fallbacks: 
- If we see false negatives (profile too narrow), presubmit router supports manual overrides via a PR label (ci/run-full-lint).
- Throttler can be disabled by setting concurrency: unlimited in .github/presubmit-config.yaml for a branch.

Checklist: 
- [x] Language-aware profiles added and lint rules scoped. 
- [x] Presubmit router implemented and unit-tested. 
- [x] Throttler binary and integration tests added. 
- [x] CI workflows updated and tested on staging. 
- [x] Rollout doc and rollback knobs added.

Related: ENG-3412 (presubmit cost reduction), ENG-4021 (CI runner stability). See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3412/language-aware-presubmit-profiles for heuristics and sample mappings.

review_comments: Alicia Park: Nice approach. Can we make the router's glob matching cacheable across CI runs? I saw some perf delta in the staging matrix.
Samir Patel: Good point — added a simple in-memory path matcher cache with a TTL and measured ~40% cheaper router evaluation on large diffs. Updated commits reflect cache addition.
Marcus Vell: Throttler looks fine but please add a metric for 'throttled_wait_seconds' so we can alert on queued latency.
Samir Patel: Added Prometheus metric 'presubmit_throttler_queue_seconds' and hooked it into the Console dashboard. Also added an alert doc to README-presubmit-rollout.md.
Priya Raman: One nit: TLS settings for the throttler's admin endpoint need to be documented for on-prem installs.
Samir Patel: Documented TLS and a disable flag for the admin endpoint in tools/presubmit-throttler/README.md.
release_notes:
- Add language-aware lint profiles to reduce presubmit runtime for single-language edits.
- Introduce a presubmit throttler to limit concurrent heavy-lint runs and stabilize CI runner usage.
- Fast-paths for docs-only and infra-only edits.
- Local preview script for teams to validate profile mapping before pushing PRs.
notes: Staged rollout started 2026-02-21 for redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-docs; monitoring dashboards show ~35% median presubmit time reduction for small edits after one week.
